plate_findings.evidence: Alternating parakeratosis and orthokeratosis in the stratum corneum in vertical and horizontal sections

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels ((a), (b)). (a): Low-magnification (×4) H&E histology of skin biopsy from left abdomen demonstrating alternating parakeratosis and orthokeratosis (checkerboard pattern) in the stratum corneum, with sparse superficial lymphocytic infiltrate, consistent with acantholytic pityriasis rubra pilaris. [raw subtype: acantholytic] (b): High-magnification (×20) H&E histology demonstrating a focus of acantholysis in the epidermis at suprabasilar and subcorneal levels, along with checkerboard pattern parakeratosis in the stratum corneum, pathognomonic for the acantholytic variant of pityriasis rubra pilaris. [raw subtype: acantholytic]

panels.figure_caption: Skin biopsy, left abdomen. Alternating parakeratosis and orthokeratosis in the stratum corneum in vertical and horizontal sections. Hematoxylin-eosin stain (a) ×4 and (b) ×20 magnification.

patchy checkerboard parakeratosis [blue arrow]

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels ((a), (b)). (a): Clinical photograph of palmar keratoderma described as psoriasiform/PRP-like in a patient with cutaneous sarcoidosis, showing orange-red erythema and scale consistent with the palmoplantar keratoderma finding in PRP. (b): H&E histology at X25 and X250 magnification demonstrating checkerboard parakeratosis, a pathognomonic histologic feature of PRP, supporting the PRP-like diagnosis in the context of the patient's cutaneous sarcoidosis.

in_text_mentions: Hair, nails, and mucus membranes examinations were normal. The differential diagnosis included mycosis fungoides, pityriasis rubra pilaris, subcutaneous lupus erythematosus, ichthyosis and psoriasis. A 4-mm punch skin biopsy was taken. The dermis revealed hyperkeratosis with checkerboard pattern of orthokeratosis and parakeratosis, the granular layer was preserved and acanthosis with thick and short rete ridges. The dermis showed mild perivascular lymphocytic infiltrates (Figure 2).
